classification.difficultyReason: Model two ordinary annuities as geometric series and compare their future values at their respective endpoints.

content.prompt:
Asam cannot decide whether to invest $\$1000$ at the end of each year for 15 years or $\$500$ at the end of each year for 30 years in a superannuation fund.

If the interest rate is $5\%$ p.a., which would be the better investment for Asam? Compare the balances at the end of their respective investment terms. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

answer.short: $\$500$ annually for 30 years gives $\$33\,219.42$, compared with $\$21\,578.56$ for $\$1000$ annually for 15 years: $\$11\,640.86$ more at the respective endpoints.
answer.worked:
Option 1: $\$1000$ at the end of each year for 15 years.

At the end of the 15th year:
$$1000(1.05)^{14}+1000(1.05)^{13}+\cdots+1000.$$
This is a geometric series with $a=1000$, common ratio $1.05$ and $n=15$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_1&=\frac{1000(1.05^{15}-1)}{1.05-1}\\FV_1&\approx\$21\,578.56\end{align*}$$
Option 2: $\$500$ at the end of each year for 30 years.

At the end of the 30th year:
$$500(1.05)^{29}+500(1.05)^{28}+\cdots+500.$$
This is a geometric series with $a=500$, common ratio $1.05$ and $n=30$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_2&=\frac{500(1.05^{30}-1)}{1.05-1}\\FV_2&\approx\$33\,219.42\end{align*}$$
Using the unrounded future values:
$$\begin{align*}FV_2-FV_1&=\frac{500(1.05^{30}-1)}{0.05}-\frac{1000(1.05^{15}-1)}{0.05}\\FV_2-FV_1&\approx\$11\,640.86\end{align*}$$
Therefore, investing $\$500$ annually for 30 years gives the greater balance at its endpoint, by $\$11\,640.86$.
